findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the max_width/max_height variant
findings.body: The PR adds a 4-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is still present. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form is gone. Any caller still using `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` now raises ArgumentError or passes the wrong arguments. The two methods should be merged into one signature, or the old one removed with all callers checked.

findings.title: Removed `dimensions` helper and changed `optimize` signature without checking other callers
findings.body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` is deleted and `optimize` now takes a preformatted dimensions string. `resize` and `downsize` were updated, but any other caller of `OptimizedImage.optimize`, `OptimizedImage.dimensions`, or the old `downsize` form (in plugins, lib, or specs) will break. The diff does not show such a search.

findings.title: Client-side size limit is hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the max_*_size_kb site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile now uses a fixed 10MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This applies to attachments too, so the `max_attachment_size_kb` setting no longer has any effect on the client. Admins who lowered the limit will see files accepted client-side and rejected only later by the server, and admins who raised it will be blocked at 10MB. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoding. This change is not mentioned in the PR description and is unrelated to downsizing images.

findings.title: Remote download cap changed from max_image_size_kb to a fixed 10MB for all uploads
findings.body: The URL download limit was `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Remote files are therefore accepted up to 10MB whatever the configured limits, and the change is not described. If the intent is to allow oversized images to be downsized, that should be stated and the limit for non-image files should still be enforced.

findings.title: Downsizing writes the output over its own input file and ignores failures
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as source and destination. ImageMagick reads and writes the same file, which is fragile and can corrupt the upload. `convert_with` returns false on failure, but the return value is ignored, so the loop just retries up to 5 times on an unchanged file. A failed conversion should stop the loop and fall through to a clear error. Writing to a separate temp file and swapping on success would be safer.

findings.title: Downsizing applies to every image type and never checks the result against the limit
findings.body: The loop only tries 5 passes, and after the loop the size is not rechecked. If the image is still over `max_image_size_kb`, the code continues to `Upload.create_for` with no explicit error, so the failure reason is unclear to the user. Also, the 80% scale is applied to non-animated formats such as SVG, where it may do nothing or produce unexpected output.

findings.title: 413 handler reports a fixed 10 MB limit that may not match the server
findings.body: The 413 case now always reports 10 MB, but the server limit comes from site settings and the web server limit is separate. The message can be wrong for the actual configuration.

findings.title: PR description is placeholder text
findings.body: The description is only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the feature, the new 10MB limits, the removal of the site-setting-driven limit on the client, or the signature change to OptimizedImage. Reviewers cannot assess the intended behavior from it.
